provenance: Original synthetic teaching cases prepared with AI assistance. No customer media or product-output benchmark is included. Expected outcomes use the supplied fictional source and the cited specifications.

sources.title: WebVTT W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft, 20 May 2026
SubRip format description, Library of Congress

cases.title: A cue ends before it starts
cases.source: Fictional onboarding. The words should appear from second 2 to second 5.
cases.explanation: The end timestamp precedes the start. The corrected interval follows the stated fictional timing. Real timing requires checking the media.

cases.title: The WebVTT header disappeared
cases.source: A standalone WebVTT caption file, intended for a player that accepts WebVTT.
cases.explanation: A standalone WebVTT file starts with the WEBVTT signature. This repair addresses the missing signature and does not verify player-specific support.

cases.title: Two speakers overlap
cases.source: Two fictional speakers talk at once between seconds 2 and 3. Preserve the simultaneous dialogue.
cases.corrected:
1
00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,000
ALEX: Can I ask a question?

2
00:00:02,000 --> 00:00:03,000
ALEX: Can I ask a question?
SAM: Yes, go ahead.

3
00:00:03,000 --> 00:00:04,000
SAM: Yes, go ahead.
cases.explanation: Overlapping cues can represent simultaneous speech. Treat an overlap warning as a review request. This two-line alternative illustrates a delivery choice and needs player and media review.

cases.title: A sentence flashes past
cases.source: The fictional speaker has six seconds for this sentence. For this exercise, the review threshold is 20 visible characters per second.
cases.broken:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:01,000
Open the learning portal and choose your onboarding course.
cases.corrected:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:06,000
Open the learning portal
and choose your onboarding course.
cases.explanation: The original cue exceeds the exercise reading-speed threshold. The threshold is an editorial assumption, not a universal format rule. The longer interval is valid only because this fictional source explicitly allows it.

cases.title: Translation reverses the instruction
cases.source: English source: Do not share your access code. Required meaning in French must preserve the prohibition.
cases.corrected:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,000
Ne partagez pas votre code d’accès.
cases.explanation: Both files are structurally plausible. The first translation reverses the instruction. A source-aware language review is needed to catch the missing negation.

cases.title: A number changes across languages
cases.source: English source: Your fictional demo invitation expires after 48 hours.
cases.explanation: The target-language number disagrees with the supplied source. Timing checks cannot establish translation accuracy.

cases.title: The same control gets two names
cases.source: Fictional product glossary: the UI label Learning hub must remain Learning hub in this French demonstration.
cases.broken:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,000
Ouvrez le Learning hub.

2
00:00:03,000 --> 00:00:06,000
Retrouvez le cours dans le centre pédagogique.
cases.corrected:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,000
Ouvrez le Learning hub.

2
00:00:03,000 --> 00:00:06,000
Retrouvez le cours dans le Learning hub.
cases.explanation: The supplied fictional glossary establishes the preferred UI label. Terminology review uses that source-specific decision. It does not make the alternative phrase wrong in every context.

cases.title: An empty cue survives export
cases.source: Fictional source has one spoken sentence from second 3 to second 6. No text is expected before it.
cases.explanation: Remove the empty cue and renumber the remaining cue for the intended SRT delivery. This exercise contains no visual or sound-description requirement for the empty interval.
